description: Same as run2_16sec_masked_pc3 but with the mask moved to 3-7s instead of 5-10s, per user request while diagnosing the 'voice breaking' issue. Fresh extraction required since the mask is baked in at extraction time, not apply time.
input_audio: same as run2: first 16s of full MDDBGospel.mp3, 16kHz mono wav

model.source_prompt: A recording of ryhtmic clapping, a women singing, and drums and guitar playing.

commands.step1_pc_extraction: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python main_pc_extract_inv.py --init_aud MDDBGospel_16sec.wav --model_id cvssp/audioldm2-music --source_prompt "A recording of ryhtmic clapping, a women singing, and drums and guitar playing." --results_path pc_extractions_masked --drift_start 150 --drift_end -1 --n_evs 3 --patch 77 179

outputs.orig.wav: true source clip, re-synthesized (mel + HiFi-GAN vocoding)
outputs.reconstruction_noPC.wav: zero-edit baseline (inversion + regeneration, same conditioning, no drift)
outputs.corrs.png: eigenvector cosine-correlation across extraction timesteps (see run1's config.json for interpretation)
outputs.MDDBGospel_pc3_a2_fixalpha.wav / a-2_fix: PC#3 applied at +-2, fix_alpha=0.025 from the start (this run never had a non-fixalpha version, since the leakage issue and its fix were already established by the time this ran)

context: Triggered by user report that the 5-10s mask version's vocal edit sounded 'weird'/broken at the exact point of the effect. This run tests whether shifting the mask window (3-7s instead of 5-10s) changes that -- e.g. if 5-10s happened to land on a difficult vocal transition (word boundary, breath, consonant) in this specific recording. Listen and compare against run2's fixalpha files directly.
not_yet_done: no amount/PC sweep run on this mask window (that diagnostic was only done for the 5-10s mask in run2b) -- if 3-7s also sounds broken at amount=2, the same sweep methodology from run2b could be applied here.
